summary: Traffic shift triggers cascade to low-throughput fallback variant causing p99 latency regressions and timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Customer observed sudden p99 latency regressions (10x) and request timeouts for inference requests during a traffic burst. Impact: Production latency increased for BrightQ Analytics' dedicated instance; several requests returned 504/timeout and streaming sessions were terminated. Initial hypothesis: routing policy incorrectly diverted a portion of traffic to a slower fallback variant that has low concurrency limits and cold KV caches.

Full impact: ~18% of requests for pinned model redwood-rlhf-1.2 saw p99 > 12s between 2026-03-13T17:02 and 2026-03-13T17:26; error rate (504) rose to 4.3% for that window. Customer reported client-side timeouts and partial transcripts lost for streaming sessions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady baseline QPS (~60 req/s) against customer route in prod-us-east for model redwood-rlhf-1.2
2) Spike traffic to ~200 req/s for 90s to simulate burst (mirror of customer's traffic pattern),
3) Observe routing decisions in routing-debug logs and per-variant concurrency metrics in Grafana
4) Notice a portion (~20%) of requests routed to variant 'fallback-slowpath-io-v1' and 'cpu-safety-fallback-2026',
5) Monitor p99 latency and error-rate for routes and variants.
observed_metrics: Variant 'fallback-slowpath-io-v1' concurrency limit observed: 6 live requests (throttled),
KV cache hit rate on fallback variants dropped to 12% (was ~86% on primary),
CPU steal / host IO wait spiked on fallback nodes by 6x concurrent with routing shift
logs: 2026-03-13T17:04:11Z routing-debug: route decision score(primary)=0.78 fallback_io_score=0.62 fallback_cpu_score=0.81 -> selected: fallback-slowpath-io-v1 (unexpected)
2026-03-13T17:05:02Z serving-runtime: replica-fallback-slowpath-io-v1: accept_request failed with KVCacheMiss=true cold_kv_warmup_in_progress=true
2026-03-13T17:07:34Z scheduler: autoscale prevented new replica creation due to quota-check fail (dedicated pool),
client: brightq-integration: session-23: stream terminated by server after 30s idle
investigation_notes: Support triage: Customer route uses pinned model + canary rollout policy with fallback allowed. Traffic spike overlap with internal autoscaler churn triggered fallback policy evaluation.

Routing rule bug: routing score comparator used stale 'estimated_latency' from last-minute probe; a recent change (PR #1289) inverted tie-breaker logic so CPU-safe variants were preferred even when not capacity-compatible.
Scheduler observed quota-check failure prevented spinning up more throughput-optimized replicas in dedicated pool due to recent quota reservation bug (INT-8842).
Result: routing diverted ~20% of new requests to low-concurrency CPU fallback variants which had cold KV caches and I/O bound path -> large p99 impact and timeouts.
Customer-side: Their client timeouts are aggressive (client-side 30s); streaming sessions were being dropped during long KV warmups.
timeline: 17:00 UTC - BrightQ reports degraded latency via support channel
17:03 UTC - Support opened ticket and escalated to SRE
17:08 UTC - Observed routing shifts in routing-debug and Grafana (variant-level)
17:14 UTC - Identified recent routing comparator change (PR #1289) that changed fallback selection tie-breaker
17:20 UTC - Temporary mitigation: disabled non-critical fallback path for BrightQ route; routed traffic to primary variants only
17:26 UTC - p99 returned to baseline for customer, errors decreased; ticket moved to investigation
comments: Aisha (Support) 2026-03-13: Customer reports spikes started at 17:02 UTC after an ad-hoc traffic surge. Attached client logs and sample request IDs.
Marco (SRE) 2026-03-13: Reproduced failure in staging by replaying traffic pattern. Noticed fallback variants have very low concurrency and long cold KV warmups.
Nina (Routing eng) 2026-03-13: Found routing comparator unit test missing for tie-breaker change in PR #1289. Preparing hotfix to revert tie-breaker inversion.
Sam (Scheduler) 2026-03-13: Quota-check bug in dedicated pool is blocking autoscaler from provisioning additional throughput replicas; filed INT-8842. Working on prioritized fix.
resolution_summary: Mitigation deployed at 17:20 UTC: disabled automatic routing to 'fallback-slowpath-io-v1' for the customer's route and temporarily raised client-side timeouts recommendation. Hotfix (revert of tie-breaker change) is queued and tested. Scheduler quota-check fix (INT-8842) will be deployed next to allow autoscaler to add throughput replicas on dedicated pools.
follow_up_actions: 1) Deploy hotfix to routing comparator to restore previous tie-breaker behavior (PR draft ready, target deploy 2026-03-14),
2) Release scheduler quota-check fix (INT-8842) to prod to allow autoscaler to scale throughput replicas under dedicated contracts,
3) Add unit/integration tests for routing tie-breaker scenarios and add a regression test in canary pipeline,
4) Update routing runbook to include 'disable-fallback' as an emergency mitigation for dedicated routes,
5) Recommend customer increase client-side streaming timeout to 60s as interim guidance and provide guidance for graceful reconnects.
